threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'—give it a few months, and you'll be seamlessly blending in with the locals.
Last night on the 133, a guy serenaded us with a ukulele. Everyone pretended to ignore him, but we all ended up humming along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found a late-night bakery with the best kaiserschmarrn, and the owner remembers my name after just two visits.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find late-night Späti DJs spinning records while you grab a beer. The blending of convenience and nightlife is unique to this city.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively avoid the Civic Center BART at night. That station's a mess; loud bangs and smoke aren't just for tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 31 Balboa, talking politics with a street performer. Only in San Francisco do you dress for the occasion while commuting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think locals only drink vermut on weekends; you’ll see us sipping it through the week at the corner bars while discussing the latest train delays.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled at the metro map, especially when the train suddenly stops and the announcements are in rapid-fire Catalan.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'thank you' to the bus driver when you get off. Everyone else just hops off like it's a personal affront.
Last night on the N133, a guy sang the entire 'Bohemian Rhapsody' and somehow got the whole bus to join in. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw my neighbor fixing an old bike with one hand while holding a baby in the other—now that's Berlin grit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find an open-air cinema showing cult classics next to a park where locals bring their own drinks and chairs. Pure summer vibes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone's a true local if they’ve seen the BART Civic Center station evacuated and shrugged it off like it's just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 47 express dressed in a full suit, balancing a performance ukulele like it was a baby. Only in the Tenderloin, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about the Gaudí spots. They miss the quiet corners where locals have coffee and gossip about last night's concert.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their bewilderment at the 'no smoking' signs in parks—still getting used to the city’s unwritten rules.
